request.spec:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A search box and a button list, over this sheet and every other sheet of its tree, every person
whose name or an alias contains the typed text (case ignored), one line per person as
<sheet id> <name> <due-total>, this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by
sheet id.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The tree search is in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What it does:** the sheet now has a search box (`search-name`) and a button (`search`). Pressing the button lists everyone whose name or an alias contains the typed text, ignoring case. Each line is `<sheet id> <name> <due-total>`. This sheet's people come first in list order, then the other sheets' people, sheet by sheet in id order. An empty search lists everyone. The `search-count` disappears when the button is pressed and comes back once the new results are in.

**Changes:**
- **Server:** a new `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree` endpoint (`tree.GET.yml`, `RespondWithTree`, `TreeResponse`). It returns the other sheets of the tree sorted by id, using the existing `SheetRepository.tree()`.
- **Front end:** a new feature in `src/main/frontend/features/treesearch/`. On each search it re-reads every sheet in the tree from the store. It works out due-totals with the same `personDueTotal` calculation the people list uses, so the numbers match each sheet's own rows.
- No data or schema changes, and no audit records, since a search changes nothing.

**Two behaviours to be aware of:**
- **"Tree" means this sheet's ancestors and descendants only.** That is how the app already defines a tree (it's what name clashes are checked against). Sister sheets, which share a parent with this one, are not searched.
- **Retired people are always included,** whether or not "Show retired" is ticked. The request says "every person" and the test doesn't settle it either way.

probe.probe_text:
I changed nothing. I read the core myself: `ClaimFigure`, `Settings`, `Claim`, `ClaimStatus`, `Person`, `Rollup`, `TakeStatement`, `ClaimNumbers`, and the front end's `rates.ts`, `claims.ts` and `people.ts`. Three read-only helpers mapped the action pipelines, the person and period rules, and the front-end figures. I spot-checked the core against them but not every line they cite.

Short paths below: Java under `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/`, front end under `src/main/frontend/features/`.

## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

### Where the screen's figures come from
- **Computed in the browser:** almost every money figure on screen. The server sends raw people, claims, rates and settings, and the front end works out `claim-due`, `person-claimed`, `person-due-total`, overdue, aging and every total itself, mainly in `rates/rates.ts`, `claims/claims.ts` and `people/people.ts`.
- **A server copy for other jobs:** the server runs a near-copy of the same rules in `claim/ClaimFigure`, `claim/Claim.counts`, `rollup/Rollup`, `statement/TakeStatement` and `period/ClosePeriod`. It uses them for audit lines, statements, settling and period closes, not for what the screen shows.

### Per claim
- **Figures sent by the server and shown as they are:** `number`, `amount`, `status`, `dueBy`, `stated`/`statedDue`, `proofs`, `batch` (settle batch), `lateEntry`, `remindedOn`, `corrects`, `deferredUntil`, `splitFrom`, `lockedBy`, `voidReason`, the status log, comments and lines (`ClaimResponse`).

- **Rate figure** (`ClaimFigure.of` / `.live`, front end `claimDue`):
  - When a statement binds the claim (`isBound`: stated and not PENDING), it is the bound figure.
  - Otherwise it is amount × the rate in force on the claim's date for the grade the person had on that date, ÷ 100, to 2 decimals.
  - `Rate.inForce` looks for the rate on the sheet, then up to 3 parent sheets (`MAX_LEVEL`). Within one sheet it takes the latest from-date on or before the claim date; if that rate's to-date has passed, the lookup falls through to the parent.
  - No rate found gives **n/a**.

- **Due** (`ClaimFigure.withLate`):
  - A settled claim shows the `settledDue` frozen when it was settled.
  - Otherwise `floored(figure + late)`: the larger of that sum and the floor in force on the claim's date (`Settings.floorOn`, default 1.00).
  - A **correction** (a negative amount that names, in `corrects`, a SETTLED claim of the same person) gets no floor and no late charge.
  - n/a stays n/a.

- **Late charge** (`ClaimFigure.late` / `lateAsOpen`):
  - Only for an OPEN or PENDING claim that is not deferred on today.
  - The overdue count starts at `Settings.overdueFrom`: the due-by plus the grace days of the claim's grade on its date.
  - For each full 30 days overdue, it adds the late % in force on that 30-day boundary date (`latePctOn`, default 0.00), charged on figure plus the charges so far, so it compounds. Each step is rounded.
  - A statement never binds the late charge; it follows the sheet's today until the claim is settled.

- **Rounding** (`Settings.rounding`): HALF_UP when the claim's `getRoundDate()` is before the policy date (the sheet's today when the policy date is blank), HALF_EVEN on or after it. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects. The front end works in whole cents (BigInt) with `roundsHalfUp`.

- **Due-by** (`Claim.fixDueBy`):
  - Set once, when the claim is built: the terms-th business day after its date, skipping weekends and holidays (`HolidayRepository.businessDaysAfter`).
  - Terms come from `Settings.termsFor`: the person's own terms, else their grade's terms on that date, else the sheet's (default 14).
  - A redate or an edit keeps the old due-by. Adding a holiday re-fixes the due-by of every claim that is not SETTLED or VOID and falls on or after the holiday (`RefixDueBys`).

- **Overdue** (`Rollup.overdue`, front end `isOverdue`): open, not deferred, and `overdueFrom` is before today.
- **Deferred** (`Claim.isDeferredOn`): OPEN and today is before `deferredUntil`.

- **Number** (`ClaimNumbers.next`, given at open by `NumberClaim`):
  - Default: `FY<yyyy>-n`, by the fiscal year of the **due-by**. The sequence is shared across the sheet's whole tree.
  - While `numbersByPeriod(today)` is on: `<period>-n` for the period containing the due-by, or `X-n` when it is in no period.
  - A number is never reused. Void, redate and merge keep the number; reassign and transfer renumber the claim (`RenumberClaim`, `TransferPerson`).

### Which claims count (`Claim.counts`, front end `counts` + `liveHolds`)
- SETTLED claims always count.
- OPEN and PENDING claims count, except when not bound by a statement and either:
  - dated inside one of the person's holds (`Person.heldOn`), or
  - the person's retirement date has been reached (`retiredOn(today)`), whatever the claim's date.
- A claim deferred on today never counts.
- DRAFT, VOID and DELETED claims never count.
- For a past date, `countsAsOf` / `countedOn` use the claim's status on that date from its log.

### Per person
- **`person-claimed`** (`sumAmounts`): the amounts of counting claims, corrections left out.
- **`person-due-total`** (`personDueTotal`, `Rollup.of`, `TakeStatement`):
  - The dues of counting claims added up, skipping n/a, each at the rate of the grade on the claim's date.
  - It is **n/a** when the person's grade today has no rate today and no counting claim is "kept". Kept means: a settled or bound figure, a figure under a different grade, or a figure dated on or before today.
  - It is then held to the cap in force on **today** (`Settings.capped`).
- **Other per-person figures:**
  - `person-excess`: how far the uncapped total goes over the cap.
  - `person-settled-total` / `person-open-total`: the same split by status, before the cap.
  - `person-overdue-count` / `-total`.
  - Aging buckets 0–30, 31–60 and 61+: days from the claim's date to today.
  - `person-active`: a counting open claim dated within the last 30 days.
  - `person-backing`: from each patron's SETTLED claims in the last 90 days, × their share.
  - `person-cut-total`: from pool cuts.
  - Per-period due-total.
  - The last three and the aging, active and excess rules exist only in the front end.
- **Patron shares** (`PersonResponse.shares`): 100.00 split equally, half-even, with the remainder going to the first patron.
- **From the server:**
  - grade (the one in force on today, `gradeOn`)
  - statement count, stated total and statement date
  - `retired` / `retiredFrom`
  - `held`: true if the person has ever had any hold, even one that has ended
  - clashing, origin, snapshots

### Sheet totals
- **Due and overdue totals** (`trimmedSumDue`, `Rollup.trimmed`): the people's figures added up, skipping n/a. With 3 or more figures, the single highest and single lowest are left out.
- **Not trimmed:** the claimed total, settled/open totals and counts.
- **The rest:**
  - Header figures, and "my" figures (the person whose name or alias matches the user).
  - Totals per tag and per month.
  - Summary per grade (retired people left out), per period and per status.
  - Consolidated figures across the sheet's descendants.
- **Audit lines:** ROLLUP, TOTALS and ALERT lines record these as they change (`Rollup.changesSince`). An ALERT is written when someone's due-total crosses above `alertThreshold`.

### What gets frozen, and when
- **Settle** freezes `settledDue`:
  - the bound figure, or the live figure, plus the late charge, raised to the floor
  - **Approve** freezes it from the live figure.
  - **Resettle** (steward) recomputes it from the live figure, ignoring any statement.
- **A statement** (`TakeStatement`):
  - binds each counting claim to its rate figure, without late charge or floor, and unbinds every other claim
  - stores the due-total (with late charge, floor and cap) and the date
  - can be taken as of a past date, using the history as it stood then
  - The binding is undone by reassign, split, a cancelled statement (steward only; earlier bindings are not restored) and clone. It is kept on merge, and re-bound on the target sheet by transfer.
- **A period close** (`ClosePeriod.fix`):
  - freezes per-person totals for claims whose **due-by** is in the period, using each claim's status on the period's end date
  - but uses today's holds, grades and late charge, and does not apply the cap
  - Reopen clears these totals.
- **On creation:** the due-by and terms are frozen, and so is `lateEntry`, which is set when the due-by is in a soft-closed period.

### Status and who may do what
- **Status moves** (`ClaimStatus.canMoveTo`):
  - DRAFT → OPEN
  - OPEN → PENDING or SETTLED
  - DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED → VOID
  - DRAFT ↔ DELETED (a restore works only on the today the claim was deleted)
  - Only a DRAFT can be edited.
- **Roles:** clerk (the default), steward, viewer. `CheckCanChange` refuses a viewer, or any change on an archived sheet.
- **Permission matrix** (`Settings.allows` / `rolesFor`): open, settle, void and close by clerk or steward; reassign and reopen by steward only, unless the settings override them.
- **Steward only, hard-coded** (each with a different exception):
  - approve and reject (`ApprovalException`)
  - resettle (`ResettleException`)
  - redate (`StewardOnlyException`)
  - cancel statement, merge, transfer, clone, archive
- **Delegation:** makes someone a steward while the sheet's today is inside the delegation window.
- **Settle rules** (`SettleClaim`):
  - Refused if the claim is deferred.
  - Refused if the user opened or last edited it (`isOwnedBy` → `SelfSettleException`).
  - Refused if `needsProof`: no proofs and the due is above the grade's, or else the sheet's, proof threshold on the claim's date.
  - A **clerk** settling a due above the clerk limit in force on **today** makes the claim PENDING instead of SETTLED.
- **Open:** refused when `needsNote` (the due is above the note threshold and the note is blank), or when the period cap is reached (`PeriodCaps.full`).
- **Void of a SETTLED claim:** steward only, within 7 days of settling (`SETTLED_DAYS`). It needs a reason from the sheet's list when the sheet has one, and must have no reason when it has none.
- **Remind:** once per today.
- **Lock:** a claim locked by another user's open editor today refuses edits (`ClaimLockedException`).

### What dates decide
- **The claim's date decides:** the rate, the grade, the floor, the late %, the terms, the proof and note thresholds, the grace days, and the rounding (against the policy date).
- **The sheet's today decides:** the late charge, overdue, deferral, `retiredOn`, the cap, the clerk limit, the person's grade shown on screen, period numbering, delegation, auto-close, and as-of history.
- **Changing today:**
  - writes a SNAPSHOT for each person
  - auto-closes every open period whose end plus `graceDays` is before the new today (`AutoClosePeriods`; never soft-closed periods, and with no role check)
- **The due-by decides:** the period a claim belongs to (for closed-period checks, numbering and period totals) and the fiscal year of its number.

### Hold, retire, closed period, import
- **Hold:**
  - changes **counting only**: unbound open claims dated inside the hold stop counting
  - blocks nothing
  - cannot be removed
  - gives a pool member no cut on days the hold covers today
- **Retire:**
  - Once the retirement date is reached, none of the person's unbound open claims count.
  - A claim dated **after** the retirement date, or inside a past retirement window, is refused (`retiredBefore`, `CheckClaimRetired`).
  - Unretire records a past retirement window.
- **Closed period:**
  - Every claim action is refused when the claim's **due-by** is in a hard-closed period (`CheckClaimPeriod` → `ClosedPeriodException`).
  - Remind, comment, unlock and the new claim from a split skip this check.
  - A soft-closed period blocks nothing and only marks new claims as `lateEntry`.
- **Import people** (`AddImportedPeople`):
  - A line is matched by name or alias. A matched person is updated: grade from today if it differs, and terms and contact only if given (a blank keeps them).
  - Name and tags are never changed. There is no version check and no retired check.
  - The first bad line, or a repeat within the import, refuses the whole import.
- **Import rates:** later lines win. A rate with the same grade and from-date is replaced.
- **Paste:** all lines are checked before any is written. Each becomes a DRAFT. Negative amounts are refused.
- **Plans:** dates refused because of a closed period or retirement are skipped silently and tried again on the next run.

### Things that look wrong
These come from reading the code; I did not run anything to confirm them:
- **Front end and back end can disagree.** They hold two separate copies of the rules. For example, `sumAmounts` uses floating point while the server uses BigDecimal, and the floor is 0.00 until settings load.
- **Doc comments disagree with the code.** The `Rollup` comment says OPEN and SETTLED count, but the code also counts PENDING.
- **The three server totals disagree on the cap.** `Rollup` and `TakeStatement` apply it; `ClosePeriod` does not.
- **Bulk actions skip checks.** They re-implement the checks inline with different subsets; for example, bulk reassign doesn't refuse moving a claim to the person who already has it.
- **Edit and add date an undated claim differently.** Edit uses today; add uses the entry date.
- **The permission system can be bypassed.** A clerk can set roles, settings and rates with no steward check, and the user is just the `X-User` header the client sends.

## 2. How hard it was to follow

It was hard: the logic is scattered and tangled, not in one place a new developer could pick up. The claim-figure core (`ClaimFigure` + `Settings`) is clear and well commented, but which claims count, the due-total and the "n/a" rule are written out separately in `Rollup`, `TakeStatement`, `ClosePeriod` and again in the front end, and that front-end copy is what the screen actually shows. Who-may-do-what is split across YAML step order, about 60 single-purpose step classes, the bulk steps' inline copies, SQL guards and 32 error-handler files, so understanding even "settle" means reading about a dozen files.
